profile.campus: Hillsboro, Oregon (Flexential's Hillsboro data center campus, four existing buildings plus a fifth completed and a sixth planned as of 2025)

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Portland - Hillsboro 1) is located at 3935 NE Aloclek Place, Hillsboro, OR 97124. The operator publishes a footprint of 85388 square feet and 5.3 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, NIST 800-53, ITAR, SSAE 18. This building is part of Flexential's wider Hillsboro campus, which Data Center Dynamics reported in 2025 had grown to five sites (four existing buildings plus Hillsboro 5, then under construction) totaling 1.18 million square feet and 113 megawatts of capacity, with a sixth facility then being planned across from Hillsboro 1 at 350,000 square feet and 27 megawatts. Flexential president and COO Ryan Mallory described Hillsboro as "a smart alternative to Silicon Valley for customers seeking the performance, flexibility, and cost structure they can't find elsewhere, especially those with strong ties across the Pacific." DCD also reported that the Hillsboro market ran extremely tight in the first half of 2025, with a vacancy rate of just 0.2% and 48.4 megawatts of absorption against 48 megawatts of new supply delivered, roughly 10% of total market inventory turning over in six months. Hillsboro sits in Oregon's "Silicon Forest" technology corridor west of Portland, built up around Intel's long-standing local manufacturing presence and the skilled workforce it created, a legacy that has also drawn other major data center operators, including Meta, to the same area.

The City of Hillsboro reports that, as of July 2026, the city hosted 23 total data center sites, 16 already constructed across 346 acres plus 7 more in permitting or under construction across another 224 acres, together occupying roughly 570 of the city's 17,378 total acres. In 2025, Hillsboro's data center sector generated about $61.1 million in total taxes; 12 entities receiving Enterprise Zone property-tax abatements held roughly $7.2 billion in exempted real market value, out of an $11 billion combined assessed/exempted value across all data centers in the city. Eligible facilities receive temporary property-tax abatement on new investment for three to five years under Hillsboro's Enterprise Zone program, after which standard property taxes apply, alongside application fees capped at $50,000 and Community Service Fees of up to 33% of abated taxes in the first three years. Statewide, Oregon's data center industry supported an estimated 9,310 direct jobs and 38,380 indirect and induced jobs, with more than $4.1 billion in labor income, in 2023, according to industry analysis cited by the city.

reading.body:
At 5.3 MW of published IT capacity across 85,388 square feet, this campus is a mid-sized colocation facility by any standard measure. To translate that power into approximate compute density: at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 5.3 MW supports roughly 130 racks, and at 10 kW per rack, a more typical mixed-workload assumption, it supports roughly 530 racks. The operator has not published a rack count, a cooling architecture, or a power density ceiling, so which of those figures is more realistic for this specific floor cannot be determined from the available data.

The certification stack qualifies this campus to host regulated workloads across several demanding frameworks. SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II satisfy financial and operational controls audits. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. ITAR qualifies it for export-controlled defense technical data. NIST 800-53 aligns it with federal information system controls. SSAE 18 is the attestation standard under which the SOC reports are issued. Together these certifications make the facility eligible for highly regulated tenants, though which tenants are actually present is not published.

Within Oregon, this site ranks seventh among the eight facilities for which published megawatt figures exist, out of 133 total mapped facilities in the state. Its 5.3 MW represents roughly 2.8 percent of the 192.6 MW published across those eight Oregon facilities, meaning the published Oregon capacity is heavily concentrated elsewhere. Oregon has 133 mapped facilities but only eight with published power figures, so the true state total is unknown and this ranking reflects only what operators have chosen to disclose.
